focus: Surface overrides, detection edges, and registry vocabulary
noveltyJustification: All five findings are fully new for this round and none repeat rounds one or two: the unowned comment budget, a live packet-number pointer, the registry description omitting Obsidian, the missing OBSIDIAN-versus-WEBFLOW collision test, and a stale link label in the Webflow enforcement file.
keyQuestions: How does stack detection behave for mixed stacks, monorepos and two-surface matches, and where do the surface packets' overrides of shared standards silently diverge?
ruledOut: Report the 3-per-10 cap as a P0 gate defect - no checker gates comments by count
Report toolSurface entries as conflicting with packet frontmatter - quality and review tool surfaces match their SKILL.md exactly
Count the stale two-surface phrasing as a wording relic - mode-registry.json is the runtime routing source of truth

label: The OpenCode surface enforces a comment budget the shared universal tier does not have and nothing measures: 'Maximum 3 comments per 10 lines of code' appears in naming-and-commenting.md:170 and in every language style guide and five checklists (14 rows across 13 files), while the shared universal guide defaults to no comments and requires one only for hidden constraints and invariants with no quantity rule, and no checker counts comments. A 10-line security block with four durable WHY comments violates the checklist row and satisfies the universal contract. Reproducing case: rg -n '3 comments per 10|max 3 comments per 10' .skilled/skills/sk-code --glob '!benchmark/**' prints 14 rows across 13 files; rg over sk-code-quality/scripts finds no count-enforcing script. NEW P2.

A live OpenCode reference carries a packet-number pointer in its own prose: naming-and-commenting.md:283 reads 'Carry-over from 139: keep rule constants centralized...' while the same file's section 4 declares ephemeral-artifact pointers forbidden and calls the rule a HARD BLOCK. The pointer sits in documentation, not a code comment, so no hook scans it, but it is the dangling-reference class the rule exists to stop. Reproducing case: rg -n 'Carry-over from' .skilled/skills/sk-code --glob '!benchmark/**' prints this one row and no other. NEW P2.

The mode registry's own description omits the third surface it registers: mode-registry.json:5 describes the surface axis as '(sk-code-webflow/sk-code-opencode)' while extensions.surface-axis.surfaces:19 lists sk-code-obsidian and the modes array carries its full entry at 98-110. The same stale two-surface phrasing recurs in shared/README.md:17. Reproducing case: rg -n 'sk-code-webflow/sk-code-opencode' mode-registry.json prints line 5. NEW P2.

No test covers an OBSIDIAN-versus-WEBFLOW collision, the one precedence decision that needs it: stack-detection.md section 4 has Webflow, Obsidian, and mixed-.skilled/ rows but none where a target set satisfies both Obsidian repo-root markers and a Webflow marker, and the canary corpus's eleven cases include no collision case. A wrong order would silently route Obsidian plugin work through Webflow standards or the reverse. Reproducing case: the fixture's cases[].id list has surface-bundle-reference, surface-bundle-obsidian, single-webflow, single-obsidian and no collision case; stack-detection.md's section 4 table carries no combined row. NEW P2.

A Webflow enforcement file keeps a stale link label while pointing at the right target: enforcement.md:310 renders a link whose label text is '../../../assets/webflow/checklists/code-quality-checklist.md' and whose target is '../../../sk-code-quality/assets/code-quality-checklist/overview-header-and-comments.md'. The target resolves, but a reader who copies the label lands on a missing file. Reproducing case: test -f .skilled/skills/sk-code/assets/webflow/checklists/code-quality-checklist.md returns no while the link target exists. NEW P2.
